findings.F1: The test's result is on the side the idea predicts but short of the bar: a |forecast|-weighted 7-day unusual fall of +1.56 % with day-clustered t 1.57 over 211 days. Its size, unusual move +1.13 % (t 2.08, 624 days, strength 0.071), is erased by the coins' normal drift of -1.13 % in the short direction, so the total move is -0.01 % against a trade cost of 0.22 %. The test already used every fold and all 19 coins, so no more data is available.
findings.F2: The effect is not graded by the depth of the fall. In folds B and C, inside choppy bars, the slope of the 7-day unusual move on the 30-day return among falls has t 0.56 (159 cases). By sextile of the 30-day return, the deepest falls (below -22 %) give +4.7 % (t 1.51, 30 days), the middle falls (-22 % to -8.8 %) only +1.2 % (t 0.41, 34 days), and the shallowest falls (-8.8 % to -1.5 %) +3.4 % (t 2.35, 38 days).
findings.F3: The clause that the fall keeps going after the coin climbs back over its 30-day-old close fails. On the 3,444 bars held short with forecast 0, the mean gain before costs is -0.022 % per bar, so the supporting check did not pass.

no_ideas: The tested fall effect is on its side but already measured on all the data (F1), and no part of it shows the effect clearly. It is not graded by depth (F2), its recovery clause loses (F3), no horizon clears the bar (F4), and the brief's rise side is absent (F5). It also fades by year and splits across coins and windows (F6), so the theme's effect is not in the data.
